Floor 34 -> 26: staging block 2's dz through the return carrier itself (with a ret=0 restore) holds the target's exact exit shape AND its sixth callee-save at the same time - s4's anti-correlation is
Floor holds at 26; the whole residual is now typed - the ret pseudo (reg 96) is allocno ORDER 0 yet carries a pre-allocation hard conflict with $v0, which prune_preferences uses to strip its $v0 copy

frontier.hypothesis: Pseudo 96's hard-register conflict with $v0 is created at a basic-block entry (flow believing hard $v0 is live at the start of blocks that reg 96 spans), not by the epilogue copy; removing it is the entire remaining residual
frontier.mechanism: global_conflicts seeds hard_regs_live from basic_block_live_at_start (global.c:695-698) and immediately calls record_conflicts (global.c:725), which IORs hard_regs_live into hard_reg_conflicts of every allocno live at that point. That path - unlike mark_reg_store, which skips FIXED registers at global.c:1502 - explains why $sp (reg 29) appears in the same conflict lines. Once the conflict is gone, prune_preferences (global.c:907-909) stops deleting reg 96's $v0 copy preference and find_reg seats ret in $v0, which collapses the trailing move v0,v1 and the whole {v0,v1,a0,a1,a2} rename against the target.
frontier.next_probe: Run the instrumented cc1 (tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1 - NOT tools/gcc-2.7.2/build/cc1) on this body with an env-guarded print of the hard-register part of basic_block_live_at_start per basic block, or of every (allocno, hard reg) pair recorded by record_conflicts / record_one_conflict, to identify WHICH block entry marks $v0 live. Then ask the C question the answer implies: which exit geometry stops flow carrying $v0 live into those blocks. Do not spend further sandbox measurements on spelling until that print exists - s6 measured eight spellings and the seat did not move once.

frontier.hypothesis: A permuter campaign seeded on q1 or q2 - the two ties at 26 that compile to a DIFFERENT object from the base - finds what the base 26 basin could not
frontier.mechanism: s5's perm_e saturated the 26 basin (11,782 iterations, 9 novel finds, every one semantically broken) but it was seeded on the base object; q1 and q2 are different source geometries that compile to different objects, so their permuter neighbourhoods are different. The standing lesson on this function is that a semantically broken find is a LEAD - both floor drops on record (40 to 34 and 34 to 26) came from hand-repairing one.
frontier.next_probe: tmp/grind/func_8002E6B0/s5/mkws.sh (it carries the current -mel -msoft-float flags; the older tools/mar_perm_workspace.sh and the func_800283D0 copy predate soft-float) on memory/grind/func_8002E6B0/rejected/s6_final_xor_swap_distinct_object_ties_26.c and .../s6_first_if_xor_swap_distinct_object_ties_26.c, one fresh-seed window each. Do NOT re-seed the base 26 basin (perm_e) or the 34 basin (s4 perm_c) - both are spent probes on the record. Read every find's SEMANTICS before scoring it.

frontier.hypothesis: tools/ra_solver's forward model can be fixed for func_8002E6B0, after which inverse.py can type the ret seat REACHABLE or FORECLOSED
frontier.mechanism: simulate.py is 11/31 on this function and every miss is concentrated in the first three allocnos (96, 95, 94), which are exactly the $v0/$v1/$a0 group - a small, well-bounded discrepancy in find_reg's pass-0 seed or in the regs_someone_prefers avoidance rather than a wholesale model failure.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run tools/ra_solver/simulate.py --trace on tmp/ra_solver_work/func_8002E6B0.model.json and compare the pass-0/pass-1 decision for pseudo 96 against the FINDREGDBG stream that extract.py already parses; the dump says $v1, the model says $a1, so the divergence is in which regs the model excludes. Only after the model reproduces ord 0-2 is inverse.py's verdict on this seat worth anything.
